title: Air India Pilot Tests Positive for Marijuana After Phuket Flight Dropped 300 Feet
excerpt: The captain of the A320neo that injured 17 people has tested positive for marijuana in a confirmatory drug test, as CEO Campbell Wilson faces government questioning.
body:
• The captain of Air India flight AI2379 has tested positive for marijuana in a confirmatory drug test, according to Reuters sources familiar with the investigation.
  • The A320neo aircraft dropped roughly 300 feet during approach to Delhi on August 4, injuring 13 passengers and four crew members, including one crew member who suffered a spinal fracture.
  • India's aviation ministry has summoned Air India CEO Campbell Wilson for questioning, and the Aircraft Accident Investigation Board has classified the incident as a "serious incident."
  • Both the captain and first officer have been taken off flight duties pending the investigation.

The captain who was flying an Air India Airbus A320neo when it suddenly lost altitude on approach to Delhi has tested positive for marijuana in a confirmatory drug test, Reuters reported on Monday, citing sources familiar with the matter.

The positive result escalates what was already a damaging episode for India's largest airline. Flight AI2379 from Phuket to Delhi, carrying 137 passengers and eight crew members on aircraft VT-EXO, dropped approximately 300 feet during approach on August 4. The jolt threw passengers into the cabin ceiling and cracked interior panels.

What Happened on Flight AI2379

Passenger accounts paint a terrifying picture. An Italian traveler told media outlets that passengers believed they were going to die during the sudden altitude loss. At least 13 passengers and four crew members were injured, with one cabin crew member sustaining a spinal fracture.

https://x.com/ShivAroor/status/2087235229694210163

"We thought we would die. People were screaming, and those without seatbelts were thrown to the ceiling."

— Passenger aboard Air India flight AI2379

Photographs from inside the cabin showed visible cracks in ceiling panels where passengers and crew struck the fuselage. The Directorate General of Civil Aviation immediately grounded both pilots and ordered drug testing after initial screening flagged the presence of psychoactive substances.

Confirmed Positive and CEO Summoned

After the initial screening raised red flags, confirmatory laboratory testing was ordered. Those results, now in hand, confirm the captain tested positive for marijuana. Air India had previously said the airline had not been informed of the test results as of August 9.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=MKsxHTMx9N0

India's aviation ministry has separately summoned CEO Campbell Wilson to explain the incident and the airline's safety protocols. The Aircraft Accident Investigation Board has classified the event as a "serious incident," a designation that triggers a formal investigation with potential regulatory consequences.

Both the captain and first officer remain off the flight roster. Air India has not publicly commented on the confirmed drug test result.

A Pattern of Drug-Related Incidents

The positive test comes against a backdrop of prior drug-related incidents involving Air India crew. In April 2026, an Air India pilot was deported from San Francisco after U.S. authorities found marijuana in his luggage. In an earlier incident in 2024, a pilot was fired after failing a breathalyzer test following a separate Phuket-to-Delhi flight.

The repeated incidents raise questions about the adequacy of Air India's pre-flight screening procedures and whether the airline's rapid post-privatization expansion under the Tata Group has outpaced its safety culture reforms.

Airbus Investigation Underway

Separately, Airbus has dispatched specialists to examine the A320neo aircraft involved in the incident. While the altitude loss could have multiple contributing factors — including weather, mechanical issues, or pilot error — the confirmed drug test result will intensify scrutiny on the human factors element of the investigation.

What Comes Next

The AAIB investigation will determine the precise cause of the altitude loss and whether the captain's marijuana use was a contributing factor. Air India faces potential regulatory action from the DGCA, which has the authority to impose fines, suspend operating certificates, or mandate enhanced screening protocols. Wilson's meeting with the aviation ministry could result in additional safety directives for the airline, which has been working to rebuild its reputation since its 2022 acquisition by the Tata Group.
